claim: For the four-dimensional flow \(\dot x=-ay-xz-u\), \(\dot y=x(z-c)\), \(\dot z=-b-mxy\), \(\dot u=kx-y\), with \(b\ne0\), define \(R=m y^2+(z-c)^2\). Along every classical solution, \(\dot R=-2b(z-c)\). Consequently, on every bounded forward solution, \(\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\int_0^T z(t)\,dt=c\); every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\int z\,d\mu=c\). Since the divergence is \(-z\), Liouville's formula gives \(\log|\det D\phi_T|=-cT+[R(T)-R(0)]/(2b)\), hence every bounded forward orbit has asymptotic phase-volume rate \(-c\), and every compactly supported ergodic invariant measure has Lyapunov-sum \(\sum_{j=1}^4\lambda_j=-c\) whenever its Lyapunov spectrum is defined. In particular, every periodic orbit has exact period mean \(c\). This upgrades the source's empirical statement that \(c\) is almost positively correlated with the offset of \(z\) to an exact stationary law and explains the reported Lyapunov sums near \(-1\) at \(c=1\) and \(-1.3\) at \(c=1.3\).
integrity: The exact balance law is obtained by direct differentiation and integration. Reported numerical Lyapunov sums are used only as consistency checks, not as proof. The source's empirical offset observation is distinguished from the exact theorem proved here.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is conditional on the printed ODE and \(b\ne0\). Bounded-orbit conclusions require bounded forward trajectories; invariant-measure claims require compact support; no attractor-existence or individual-Lyapunov-exponent claim is made. The 2014 three-dimensional precursor was available only through abstract/bibliographic material in the inspected lawful sources, leaving a residual risk that it discussed a fixed-parameter special case.
title: Exact mean-height and phase-volume law for a controllable hyperchaotic hidden-attractor flow
